samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim second copy of `readOnlyDocStore` (same Proxy traps, same memoization, same rationale comments) instead of a shared helper
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts reimplements every trap of packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts (`get` with the non-configurable/non-writable exception, `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty` → false, `getPrototypeOf` → null, `setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions` → false, `isExtensible` → true, `has`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `ownKeys` filtered by `configurable === false`, the memoizing `members` map, the `batch(fn)` special case) with only the readers allowlist and `HISTORY_METHODS` genuinely new. No shared primitive exists (`Grep 'Proxy' packages/core/src` → no matches), and notes does not depend on `@wafflebase/core` (packages/notes/package.json), so this repo's stated reuse expectation was available (a generic `readOnlyStoreView(store, readers, overrides)` in core, or in either engine's shared util) but not taken. Cost: this is an escape-resistant guard duplicated across two packages — a trap hardening or bug fix applied in one (as happened historically for `setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions` in the docs copy) will silently not apply to the other, giving two different answers to "can a viewer reach the raw CRDT handle?".

samples.summary: The docs sibling still asserts the claim this change explicitly repudiates ("with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary"), so the two wrappers' documented meaning now contradict each other
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42 says the shadow-mode webhook makes the proxy "the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one". The new notes wrapper (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:52-70) and docs/design/notes/notes.md (§"What that wrapper is not") declare exactly that reasoning wrong, and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md's new Risks bullet names `readOnlyDocStore` as a correctness boundary only. The corrected reasoning was applied to notes and to the design docs but not to the docs package's own comment, leaving the canonical statement of the same fact in two places disagreeing.

samples.summary: Backend changes (boot-time posture logging, shadow-log target field) and the new `yorkie-auth-webhook.md` Risks bullet are outside the originating issue's scope
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md lists the whole scope as N1–N8 (toolbar mount, mobile demotion, viewer toolbar, token uploader, session-local prefs, no member branch) plus "3 — engine divider touch target" and "4 — delete the obsolete rationale comments; correct docs/design/notes/notes.md"; "Out of scope" names only sheets/board. `logPosture()` and the `target=` field in the shadow log (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120-158) are a separate backend observability change riding along. Defensible as fallout from the corrected read-only claim, but it widens the review surface of a frontend parity fix; cost stays inside the codebase.

samples.summary: The notes preference/mobile-demotion state machine is now copied into a second component rather than shared
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:90-139 owns `viewMode`/`keymap`/`showAuthors` and the `isMobile && viewMode === "both" ? "edit" : viewMode` demotion; shared-notes-layout.tsx:48-70 repeats both, differing only in the absence of the `write*` calls. The demotion rule is a documented product behaviour (docs/design/notes/notes.md §Mobile, and the toolbar comment now points at both routes), so a future change to it must be made twice or the two entry paths diverge again — which is precisely the class of bug issue #1044 was filed for. A small shared hook (e.g. `useNotePreferences({ persist })`) was available.

samples.summary: The reused docs uploader has a different failure contract from the notes `uploadImage` contract, so a share-link editor's failed upload is reported only to the console
samples.evidence: `UploadImage` in packages/notes (view/editor.ts:218-224) is documented as resolving `null` when "the host handled the failure itself", and the workspace path does exactly that with a toast (notes-detail.tsx:208-231). `shareTokenImageUploader` returns `DocsImageUpload = (file) => Promise<string>` and rejects on failure (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49); packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190 swallows the rejection into `console.error`. So N5's "behaves as it does for a member" (docs/design/notes/notes.md:447-451) is only partly true: the placeholder vanishes with no user-visible error for a share-link editor. Reuse is right; the missing adapter (catch → toast → `null`) is the gap.

samples.summary: Design docs record review-conversation meta ("An earlier draft of this section claimed… That was wrong") rather than the current design
samples.evidence: docs/design/notes/notes.md adds a "**What that wrapper is not.** An earlier draft of this section claimed…" paragraph, and packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:52 similarly narrates "the earlier claim here … was wrong". The correction itself is valuable and correctly folded into the canonical subsystem doc (no parallel doc added), but the draft-history framing is not the shape docs/design/template.md asks for; stating the two boundaries and their preconditions without the retraction narrative would age better.

samples.summary: The read-only store is wrapped twice (frontend mount and `initialize()`), relying on idempotence to make the redundancy harmless
samples.evidence: notes-view.tsx:152 wraps with `readOnlyNoteStore` and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:249 wraps again; the `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` WeakSet exists solely so the second wrap is a no-op. Defensible as defence-in-depth (the frontend keeps its own handle for `getText()`), but the engine wrap alone would cover the engine, and the extra layer plus the idempotence machinery is coupling the two callers to an invariant neither can observe.

verdict.reason: The claimed duplication is present exactly as described. packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93-185 reimplements every trap of packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 — the get non-configurable/non-writable exception (notes:112-115 vs docs:84-87), data-property hiding (notes:117 vs docs:96), the memoizing members map (notes:98,119-120,146 vs docs:71,98-99,119), the batch(fn) run-the-body case (notes:127-136 vs docs:104-112), set/defineProperty/deleteProperty to false, getPrototypeOf to null, setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions to false, isExtensible true (notes:149-155 vs docs:122-141), and byte-equivalent has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys filtered on configurable===false (notes:159-180 vs docs:147-167). Only the readers allowlist (notes:19-27), HISTORY_METHODS (notes:35) and the READ_ONLY_VIEWS WeakSet (notes:43) are new. No shared primitive exists (Grep 'Proxy' in packages/core/src returns no matches), while a shared home was available since packages/docs/package.json:56 already depends on @wafflebase/core. Divergence is already concrete: the notes copy has the idempotency WeakSet the docs copy lacks, so two copies of the same escape-resistance guard already answer differently — matching the rubric's major bar for duplicated logic that will diverge and give two answers to the same question. Both copies are live and reachable (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts), so no guard or scope argument removes it.
